hook_text: A truck of crushed bottles goes in one door. Bags of clean plastic rice come out the other. Here is the middle.
clip_script: A recycling plant eats bales of dirty PET bottles and makes pellets. Six steps. Cut the bale and sort: anything not PET out, clear and coloured apart. Strip the labels. Chop into flake. Hot wash with caustic soda, then a water tank where PET sinks and cap plastic floats off. Dry it hard, because wet flake breaks down in the melt. Then an extruder screw melts it at 270 degrees, squeezes it through a screen and a die, the strands cool in water and a knife chops them into rice. Test, bag, sell. The systems diagram is three boxes: input bales, process those six steps, output pellets, with an arrow from the tests back to the process. Resources in from the top, waste out below. Same diagram for your own design project.
visual_style: Whiteboard conveyor with bale, sorting hands, drum, granulator, wash tank with sinkers and floaters, drier, extruder with strands into water, knife, bag of pellets; then three boxes with a feedback arrow.
pacing: In, out, six steps, three boxes, feedback.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a systems diagram for anything made at home, from bread to a school project.
